findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax (for example, `main; <command>`), `exec` evaluates it in a shell and runs the injected command with the current process's privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` passed the value as one literal Git argument, so this PR introduces the injection boundary. Preserve argument-separated process execution.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve direct ownership of the Git child
findings.body: When a caller cancels a slow `git show` through the returned `ChildProcess`, `exec` represents the intermediate shell rather than Git. On POSIX, killing that shell does not reliably terminate its spawned Git process or helpers, which can continue consuming CPU and repository I/O; `execFile` made Git the directly owned child.
